name: CaseGPT: A Case Reasoning Framework Based on Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.07913 (cs.IR); the paper states 'Submitted to ICCBR' but no acceptance / proceedings publication is confirmed
authors_affiliation: Rui Yang (single author), University of California, Riverside, USA
code_url: N/A (no official code repository released; the paper provides no code link and no GitHub repo could be located)
task_domain: Domain-specific case retrieval + decision-support / insight generation for case-based reasoning (CBR) in healthcare (medical diagnosis) and legal (precedent retrieval) domains; framed as semantic information retrieval (cs.IR) rather than agentic planning.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent retrieval-and-generation system over a static curated case repository. Given an imprecise / natural-language professional query (e.g., symptom description or legal fact pattern), the system performs semantic ('fuzzy') retrieval of relevant historical cases and then generates insights/recommendations. Supervision: experiments use a held-out 20% test split with generated test queries; no interactive/online learning is tested (the paper explicitly notes it did not test learning/adaptation over time). Two domains evaluated separately (medical: 100,000 cases; legal: 50,000 case summaries).
what_is_retrieved: Full cases (problem-solution records): medical cases (symptoms, diagnostic procedures, final diagnoses, treatment outcomes) and legal court-case summaries (facts, relevant statutes, court decisions, outcomes). Treated as CBR cases.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (a curated dense-vector-indexed case database). The paper mentions incremental/dynamic index updates to add new cases, but no agent-written episodic memory of its own experiences is used during reasoning; effectively static-corpus RAG.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective (retrieve top-N most semantically relevant cases, evaluated at Precision@10 / Recall@10 / NDCG@10), augmented with a Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) diversity step; not a minimal-complete-set or precision-driven variable-size objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse]; Revise and Retain are not implemented (no case adaptation/revision loop and no learned retain step are evaluated). Reuse is realized as LLM-based insight generation conditioned on retrieved cases. Flags: Retrieve=yes, Reuse=partial (insight generation, not explicit solution transfer), Revise=no, Retain=no.
explicit_cbr_grounding: Partial. The work explicitly frames itself as 'case-based reasoning' and uses CBR terminology and keywords, and was submitted to ICCBR, but it does NOT cite the canonical CBR foundations (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner); it realizes CBR Retrieve/Reuse mechanisms under a RAG framing.
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution record / full case document): a complete medical case or a complete legal case summary, encoded as a single dense vector.
index_source: Static curated corpus, offline-induced (cases encoded once into a dense vector index). Supports incremental real-time index updates to add new cases, but is not an online experience/episodic memory grown from the agent's own outputs.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index built with the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph for approximate nearest-neighbor search; vectors of ~768-1024 dimensions; FAISS used for similarity search. (HNSW is internally a navigable-small-world graph used as an ANN index, not a semantic/dependency knowledge graph.)
retriever_type: Dense retriever (BERT-variant embeddings fine-tuned on domain corpora; e.g., LEGAL-BERT/BioBERT-style domain encoders) with cosine similarity over a FAISS/HNSW index; not BM25, not generative, not LLM-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Off-the-shelf / pretrained encoders fine-tuned on domain-specific corpora (the BERT-variant encoder is fine-tuned on legal/medical text). The retriever itself is NOT trained with contrastive similarity labels, LM-feedback, RL, or downstream task reward; selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-k plus heuristic re-ranking. [uncertain] on exact fine-tuning protocol details.
query_construction: Raw user query is parsed and encoded by a pre-trained LLM (e.g., GPT-3 or domain variant) into high-dimensional semantic vectors (tokenize-and-encode). Query expansion is applied in the insight-generation stage to capture related concepts not explicitly mentioned. Encoding is per-word/per-token then aggregated into an encoded query.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at query time): a single query is encoded and used to retrieve cases once; there is no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying loop.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (single retrieval pass per query before insight generation).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always triggered once per incoming user query; no confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: Yes. Initial cosine-similarity ranking followed by a multi-factor re-ranking step incorporating domain-specific factors (case recency, citation frequency, jurisdictional relevance), inspired by learning-to-rank; plus an MMR diversity-aware selection step. Not a cross-encoder.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + diversity filtering (MMR) + context aggregation/summarization. After retrieval, a hybrid summarization aggregates retrieved cases and query into a weighted context (attention-inspired weighting scheme) before LLM generation; no explicit distractor-filtering or reason-in-documents distillation is described.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; items are cases). Cases are encoded with a domain-fine-tuned BERT-variant encoder; no synthetic-query or weighted-field tool engineering.
index_content_separation: N/A (no separation of a lightweight index from heavy on-demand content is described; the dense vector index points to full cases).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / external API protocol). The case index does support incremental/real-time updates for new cases, but there is no MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling tool integration.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved cases are aggregated into context and injected into an LLM prompt for conditional generation (case adaptation in the loose sense of generating insights/recommendations grounded in retrieved cases). Insights are then iteratively refined by the LLM.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (one-shot retrieve-then-reason): retrieval happens once, then the LLM generates insights conditioned on retrieved cases. No planning/tree-search/MCTS, no per-step interleaving; this is a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline, not a planner.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single retrieval feeds a single generation/insight pass per query (with internal iterative refinement of the generated insight, but no additional retrieval interleaving).
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation: retrieved cases are used as context for LLM conditional generation of insights/recommendations, then iteratively refined by the LLM (IterativeRefine). No execution-feedback-driven or critic-guided revision, no RL reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved case text aggregated/summarized into a weighted free-text context that is injected into the generation prompt; output insights are free-text recommendations.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw cases (full problem-solution case records); no distillation into strategies/guidelines/workflows/skills before retrieval. Abstraction (pattern discernment) happens only downstream in the insight-generation LLM.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Limited / mostly implicit: MMR diversity-aware retrieval and multi-factor re-ranking aim to surface more relevant/diverse cases, and an attention-inspired context weighting prioritizes pertinent information; there is no explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, retriever-aware training, or distractor-aware SFT for noise robustness.
memory_type: none (static external case knowledge base / retrieval index; not an agent episodic, skill-library, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory). [uncertain] whether incremental index updates should count as growing memory; treated as a static corpus here.
write_back: No (false). The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills generated from its own reasoning back into memory; the index can be updated by adding externally-provided new cases (incremental indexing) but the system does not write back its own outputs/experiences.
online_growth: Largely no for the evaluated setting. The index supports incremental real-time updates to integrate newly supplied cases, but the paper explicitly did not test learning/adaptation over time and the agent does not grow the store from its own deployment experiences.
write_back_trigger: Never (for the agent's own experiences). New cases may be added via external incremental indexing, but there is no success/failure/reflective write-back of generated insights or solved queries.
failure_experience_usage: Not used. The corpus contains historical cases with outcomes, but failed/negative experiences are not specifically stored or retrieved as a contrastive/corrective mechanism; retrieval is success-agnostic similarity matching.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at most (new cases can be incrementally added to the index); stored case entries are not mutated, deduped, refined, or pruned. No experience-memory evolution.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-k plus heuristic multi-factor re-ranking and MMR; it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, no soft Q-learning, no preference/value-based retrieval training).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent system with a single shared static case database; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing (federated/collaborative learning is only listed as future work).
benchmarks: Two private real-world datasets assembled by the author: (1) Medical dataset of 100,000 anonymized medical cases from a large urban hospital network (symptoms, diagnostics, diagnoses, outcomes; ICD-10 standardized); (2) Legal dataset of 50,000 court-case summaries across criminal/civil/administrative law (facts, statutes, decisions, outcomes). No public/standard benchmark is used.
benchmark_family: Domain-specific information retrieval (medical IR and legal case retrieval) on private custom datasets; does NOT map to standard agentic-RAG families (not QA/multi-hop/web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL benchmarks). Closest normalized label: domain IR / CBR retrieval.
baselines: TF-IDF + BM25; BERT-based dense retrieval; GPT-3 zero-shot (retrieval + insight generation); LEGAL-BERT (legal domain); BioBERT (medical domain). For insight-generation human evaluation, only GPT-3 zero-shot is compared.
key_metrics: Precision@10 (P@10), Recall@10 (R@10), F1, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), NDCG@10, Response Time (s); plus human evaluation of generated insights on a 5-point Likert scale across Quality, Relevance, Actionability.
headline_result: Medical domain: CaseGPT reaches P@10=0.90, R@10=0.88, F1=0.89, MRR=0.92, NDCG@10=0.91 at 0.5s, vs best baseline BioBERT (F1=0.81), reported as a ~15% F1 improvement over traditional methods. Legal domain: P@10=0.93, R@10=0.90, F1=0.91, MRR=0.94, NDCG@10=0.93 at 0.8s, vs best baseline LEGAL-BERT (P@10=0.87), reported as a ~12% precision improvement. Insight quality (Likert): CaseGPT 4.3/4.5/4.4 vs GPT-3 zero-shot 3.6/3.4/3.5.
ablations: No controlled component ablations are reported. The paper provides baseline comparisons (TF-IDF+BM25, BERT, GPT-3 zero-shot, domain BERTs) and a separate human evaluation of insight generation vs GPT-3 zero-shot, but it does not isolate the contribution of individual modules (e.g., MMR diversity, multi-factor re-ranking, domain fine-tuning, iterative refinement) via ablation.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes (partially). Intrinsic retrieval-ranking metrics (P@10, R@10, F1, MRR, NDCG@10) are reported separately from the downstream insight-generation quality (human Likert evaluation of Quality/Relevance/Actionability); however there is no separate end-to-end task-success metric beyond retrieval and the human insight assessment.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed: retrieval ranking quality (MRR/NDCG, a process/ranking signal) and final insight quality (human Quality/Relevance/Actionability) are both measured; no step-wise reasoning faithfulness or trajectory-quality metrics (single-pass system).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports response time as the efficiency metric: CaseGPT 0.5s (medical) and 0.8s (legal), faster than baselines (BioBERT 0.8s, LEGAL-BERT 0.9s, TF-IDF+BM25 1.0-1.2s, GPT-3 zero-shot 1.2-1.3s). No API cost, token-count, or rollout/retrieval-call counts are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k retrieval (metrics reported at k=10, P@10/R@10/NDCG@10); retrieved set is N cases selected via MMR. No explicit token/prompt budget for the injected context is reported; an attention-inspired weighting scheme prioritizes context but k appears fixed rather than adaptive. [uncertain] on exact N / prompt token budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a system/method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Two author-assembled private datasets: medical = 100,000 anonymized real hospital-network cases (ICD-10 standardized); legal = 50,000 court-case summaries (standardized legal taxonomy). 80/20 stratified train/test split; test queries are synthetically generated to simulate real-world usage. Relevance/answer verifiability is via curated case labels + human-expert insight rating; datasets are not public, limiting reproducibility. [uncertain] on exact relevance-label construction.
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG, Lewis et al.); BERT and domain-adapted encoders (LEGAL-BERT, BioBERT); GPT-3 / LLMs; FAISS for ANN similarity search; HNSW indexing; Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) for diversity; learning-to-rank for re-ranking.
contrasts_with: Traditional exact keyword/database query systems (TF-IDF + BM25); plain BERT-based dense retrieval; GPT-3 zero-shot used directly for retrieval+generation; standalone domain encoders (LEGAL-BERT, BioBERT). Positioned as semantic, context-aware fuzzy retrieval + insight generation that outperforms keyword-based and simple LLM-based systems.
lineage: Group D (case-based planning / case-based reasoning). An early, lightweight LLM+RAG-for-CBR application paper: it implements the Retrieve (and a loose Reuse via insight generation) phases of the CBR cycle using dense-vector RAG, applied to healthcare and legal case retrieval; sits in the CBR-meets-RAG line of work but without learned retrieval policy, case adaptation/revision, or experiential memory growth.
